title: Focus Band Allocation and Soft-Freeze Trigger Matrix for Cycle Planning
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a concrete operational playbook (matrix + checklist) that tells PMs, Eng leads, and Design how to allocate 'focus bands' across concurrent initiatives for a two-week cycle, and when to trigger a soft-freeze and reserved surge lanes. The goal is to reduce last-minute descope churn, make staff hedges explicit, and provide a deterministic mechanism for partial delivery vs full cut decisions that maps to OKR risk and customer impact.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page matrix that maps remaining story points, critical-path owners, and contingency lanes to a soft-freeze signal (green/amber/red)
Clear escalation flow: who approves soft-freeze releases, who authorizes surge, and how rollbacks are handled
Playbook includes example scenarios (low-risk descope, high-risk customer blocker, infra SLO regression) with recommended actions
PM & Eng leads sign-off in weekly triage meeting and a linked Confluence doc exists
Two simulated cycle-triage tabletop exercises documented and outcomes recorded in the ticket
progress_updates: 2025-02-10: Draft proposal created after cycle retro; outlined concept and initial criteria for focus bands
2025-02-11: Shared with Eng & Design leads; initial feedback: prefer explicit token-cost/latency thresholds when infra reasons trigger soft-freeze
2025-02-12: Cost modeling run with runtime team — tradeoff: larger reserved surge reduces customer impact but increases cost by estimated 8% per cycle
2025-02-14: Incorporated design patterns for degraded UI states during partial deliveries; updated matrix with UX acceptance checks
2025-02-16: PM sync: agreed on green/amber/red thresholds and an emergency rollback owner for each initiative
2025-02-18: Draft matrix and playbook submitted for SM/Director review (this ticket moved to In Review)
decisions: Adopt three focus bands (Core, Secondary, Backfill) mapped to OKR priority and customer-impact tiers
Soft-freeze triggers will be evaluated on a daily basis starting at day -3 before release window; amber requires mitigation plan, red requires approval to continue
Reserve surge lanes will be funded as fractional FTEs (0.1-0.3) rather than full headcount to limit cost while preserving responsiveness
When infra SLOs degrade, the default action is scope rollback of non-critical features unless a written exception is approved by infra SRE lead
